text:
While the red spittle of grapeshot

whistles, furrowing the blue sky, day after day,

and, scarlet or green, near the laughing king

battalions sink, set aflame in masses;


while an unbridled madness crushes

and turns a thousand men into smoking loam;

poor dead! sunk in summer, in the grass,

in your joy, Nature, who created them holy,


there is a God who laughs among the damasks

of the altar, at incense, at chalices of gold,

who, rocked by Hosannas, sweetly falls asleep.


But he starts awake when mothers yoked

to anguish and weeping beneath their black caps

offer him a farthing wrapped in their handkerchief.

translation.title: Evil
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the antiwar contrast between slaughtered soldiers, ritual luxury, and grieving mothers.
